CETA (Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, ss. 354, 462.3 and 462.31; United Nations Act (sanctions regulations); Special Economic Measures Act (sanctions regulations); FINTRAC sectoral AML/CFT guidance. Provincial: Partnership Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 348, as amended, including the Limited Partnership transparency register regime effective 2024; applicable BC Registry regulations governing transparency reporting for limited partnerships; analogue guidance derived from the Business Corporations Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 57 transparency register framework.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (private transparency register filed with the BC Registrar of Companies; not a public searchable registry; accessible to FINTRAC, the Canada Revenue Agency, law enforcement and designated regulators upon lawful request; financial institutions and prescribed persons receive limited access for AML/CFT verification)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: British Columbia Notary Public or licensed lawyer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by Global Affairs Canada (Canada a party to the Hague Apostille Convention since 11 January 2024)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: BC Registries and Corporate Registry (Government of British Columbia)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by Global Affairs Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Appointment of Attorney for Service / In-British-Columbia registered agent designation for non-resident partners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: British Columbia Notary Public or licensed lawyer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by Global Affairs Canada

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of every proposed general and limited partner, and every individual owning or controlling 25% or more of the limited partnership, against: FINTRAC Politically Exposed Persons (domestic, foreign, and Heads of International Organizations) categories; the UN Consolidated Sanctions List; the Consolidated Canadian Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act; the OFAC SDN List as a cross-border banking benchmark; Canadian federal and provincial criminal/civil asset-freeze lists; and reputable adverse-media and litigation databases. Any PEP, HIO, sanctions hit, or high-risk-jurisdiction nexus triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and senior-management approval. All screening results must be recorded in a FATF-aligned onboarding file retained no less than five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registry Services (bcregistry.ca) and the OneStop Business Registry (onestop.gov.bc.ca); statutory corporate/partnership name search and name reservation administered by the BC Registrar of Companies via the Corporate Registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory names must be expressed in English or French using Latin alphabet letters, Arabic numerals, and a permitted limited punctuation set. Non-Latin or foreign-script names are inadmissible and must be transliterated into an English or French form. The proposed name must contain a distinctive element, a descriptive element, and a mandatory legal element: 'Limited Partnership' or the abbreviation 'LP' / 'L.P.' at the end. French-language names are accepted but BC Registry processes are conducted principally in English.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: BC name reservations are not renewable or extendable within the 56-day window; upon expiry the applicant may file a new name reservation at the statutory fee if the name remains available. If the Registrar refuses a name, the applicant may file a written Request for Reconsideration with the BC Registrar of Companies within 30 days of the refusal, supplying comparative names, trademark evidence, and supporting distinctiveness arguments. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may pursue judicial review before the Supreme Court of British Columbia. Parallel resubmission of alternative cleared names is permissible at the standard filing fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only when a licensed BC agent maintains a physical street address in British Columbia as registered office and records office; a pure mail-forwarding or non-physical virtual office is not compliant. General partners must maintain a substantive connection to British Columbia, and CRA commercial-substance expectations require verifiable operational controls, decision-making records, and contract-management infrastructure for a cloud-based LegalTech SaaS.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate for a low-risk cloud-delivered service; quantified annual probability of an unannounced CRA business-verification visit or BC Registrar compliance inspection is estimated at 10-20%. The likelihood increases materially where the registered office is a high-density multi-tenant virtual-office address or where pass-through filings show disproportionate foreign-source income.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c. 348, including sections 51 to 56 concerning limited partnership formation, registration, amendments, and cancellation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: British Columbia Registries and Online Services, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership filed with the Registrar of Companies in the prescribed form.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a British Columbia limited partnership. No statutory escrow account is required. Capital contributions, profit allocations, withdrawal rights, and additional funding obligations should be stated in the limited partnership agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The partners resolve that the Limited Partnership be registered under the Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c. 348, with the registered office and records office stated in the filed Declaration of Limited Partnership. The partners approve the limited partnership agreement, the agreed capital contributions, and the allocation of partnership interests. The General Partner is authorized to execute and file all registration documents, obtain applicable business licences, open bank and payment accounts, and enter contracts within the approved business scope. The partners acknowledge that an LP has no statutory board of directors; governance authority rests with the General Partner under the partnership agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: British Columbia Registries and Online Services, Corporate Registry, through BC Registry application channels.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select the general partner and limited partner or partners, determine contribution commitments and ownership percentages, and confirm that the proposed name complies with British Columbia naming rules. Submit a name request if a reserved business name is required. Maintain written evidence of consent for any protected or third-party name element.
required_dossiers: General partner legal name and address
Limited partner legal names and addresses
Business purpose and principal business address
Identification and authorization records for filing representatives
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, revise the name or file under an approved numbered designation. If information is incomplete, respond through the registry channel with corrected partner, address, or authorization details.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: No government pre-approval is required; preparation is undertaken by the partners and their legal advisers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute a written limited partnership agreement before or contemporaneously with registration. Define the general partner's authority, limited partner liability protections, contributions, distributions, allocations, transfer restrictions, admission and withdrawal procedures, indemnities, records, dispute resolution, dissolution, and tax reporting responsibilities. Obtain corporate or individual execution authority and retain signed originals.
required_dossiers: General partner constitutional documents and incumbency evidence
Limited partner identification and beneficial ownership information
Registered office and records office details
Signing authority resolutions or powers of attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct execution defects, obtain missing partner approvals, and re-execute inconsistent provisions. Amend the agreement before filing where the proposed terms conflict with mandatory provisions of the Partnership Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: British Columbia Registries and Online Services, Corporate Registry, via the applicable online limited partnership registration service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the prescribed registration filing with the partnership name, general partner information, registered office, records office, and other required particulars. Pay the applicable provincial filing fee in Canadian dollars. Upload or submit supporting documents where requested. Notarization is generally not required for a standard electronic filing, but foreign execution documents, powers of attorney, or registry-requested affidavits should be notarized and, where applicable, legalized or apostilled.
required_dossiers: Partner information required by the registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to a registry query within the stated deadline, correct rejected fields, replace unacceptable attachments, and resubmit the filing. Preserve the query, corrected filing, and payment record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Registration Evidence and Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: British Columbia Corporate Registry and the Canada Revenue Agency.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download and retain the certificate or confirmation of limited partnership registration and registry profile. Apply to the Canada Revenue Agency for a Business Number and any required program accounts, including GST/HST, payroll, or information-return accounts. Confirm partnership tax filing obligations and non-resident withholding requirements based on activities, partners, and payments.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct CRA identity, address, or representative-authority issues through the CRA business enquiry process and submit any requested supporting evidence. Escalate unresolved registration issues through authorized tax counsel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Relevant British Columbia municipality or regional district and, where applicable, the applicable Indigenous or federal authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the principal place of business requires a municipal business licence, zoning confirmation, home-occupation approval, signage approval, or occupancy permit. For a cloud LegalTech SaaS operation without physical manufacturing, document the premises classification and retain evidence of any licence exemption or approval. Register applicable privacy, employment, and electronic-commerce compliance processes separately from LP formation.
required_dossiers: Municipal business licence application or exemption record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to municipal deficiency notices, amend the premises use, obtain required occupancy approvals, or relocate operations to compliant premises before commencing regulated activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internal partnership governance under the Partnership Act and the limited partnership agreement.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain the executed agreement, amendments, partner register, contribution ledger, beneficial ownership records, financial statements, tax filings, contracts, and written partner approvals. Record material decisions of the General Partner and obtain limited partner consents where contractually required. File changes to registrable information with the Corporate Registry within applicable statutory periods.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inaccurate records, execute ratifying resolutions, file registry amendments, and obtain legal advice where an omission may affect limited liability, tax compliance, or third-party reliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No provincial industrial licensing board is ordinarily required for cloud document automation and electronic-signature software services. Municipal licensing authorities and sector-specific regulators may apply based on premises, services, and data activities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No provincial manufacturing or industrial operating permit ordinarily applies. A municipal business licence may be required by the municipality or regional district where the business operates.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy, Environmental Assessment Office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt for ordinary software development, cloud administration, and electronic-signature services with no prescribed reviewable project or industrial facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, industrial VOC, or manufacturing waste thresholds ordinarily apply to a standard office or cloud-services operation. General requirements remain applicable to any actual discharge, hazardous materials, electronic waste, fuel storage, wastewater system, or contracted data-centre activity. The operator must use compliant waste contractors and ensure that third-party data-centre operators hold applicable environmental permits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No industrial civil-defence clearance or structural load inspection is ordinarily required for a standard office-based SaaS business. The premises must comply with applicable municipal building, occupancy, fire-code, workplace-safety, emergency-planning, and occupational-health requirements. WorkSafeBC registration may be required for covered employers, and specialized inspections apply if the business operates server rooms, generators, battery systems, or other regulated equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) with primary portal at canada.ca/cra
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities register for a Business Number (BN) via the CRA online portal or by mailing Form RC1 if establishing a permanent establishment or making taxable supplies in Canada. The BN constitutes the statutory tax identification number (TIN) for GST/HST and related federal filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available; limited partnership status defaults to pass-through treatment. Hybrid mismatch relief may apply under domestic or treaty-based rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual taxable supplies within Canada
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: GST/HST registrants must file returns electronically via the CRA My Business Account portal. Real-time fiscal clearance, API requirements, and digital stamping are not mandated, though electronic records retention is compulsory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada or services performed outside Canada qualify for zero-rating under the Excise Tax Act; offshore services to non-residents are also eligible when export criteria are satisfied.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger penalties up to 200 percent of evaded GST, plus interest and potential criminal prosecution under the Excise Tax Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), the sole issuing and monetary authority for the Canadian dollar, complemented in the foreign-exchange and payments perimeter by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), Payments Canada, and the Department of Finance Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada is an IMF Article VIII member and an OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements adherent; the CAD is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts under the Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52). No exchange-control approval, repatriation licence, surrender ratio, or balance-sheet FX cap applies to a British Columbia limited partnership. Profit remittance and cash distributions to non-resident limited partners are unrestricted at the clearing level, subject only to Canadian income tax allocation to the partners and, where relevant, Part XIII withholding on passive-type payments. For non-Canadian founders injecting seed capital into the CA_LP, the Investment Canada Act imposes a post-establishment s.12 notification for a new Canadian business, while high-value M&A review thresholds (currently above C$1.5 billion enterprise value for WTO investors in non-cultural sectors) are not relevant to the stage-4 treasury configuration of this LegalTech SaaS structure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None exist. Canada maintains no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no export-proceeds repatriation obligation. Export or SaaS-service receipts denominated in foreign currency may be retained in a foreign-currency account or converted at the prevailing market rate without central-bank approval. Record-keeping obligations apply only under the Income Tax Act (books and records) and the PCMLTFA/FINTRAC regime, including an Electronic Funds Transfer Report where a single incoming or outgoing wire reaches the C$10,000 threshold.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (CAD) and Operating Account (CAD/USD)
Operating Account (CAD/USD) with cross-border U.S. dollar sweep
Capital Escrow Account (CAD) and Operating Account (CAD/USD)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Practically rated Medium for Canadian-regulated fintechs and payment-service providers that are registered or recognised under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RCAA) with the Bank of Canada or that participate in Payments Canada; rated Low for offshore digital EMI accounts. Canada does not recognise the EU or UK EMI passport, and no offshore EMI can hold a Lynx or ACSS settlement account. The workable treasury stack for this LegalTech SaaS is: user card payments through Stripe (settling domestically in Canada) or a licensed Canadian PSP, followed by automated clearing to the Schedule-I primary operating account, rather than maintaining corporate cash at an offshore EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For the CA_LP structure, the General Partner or the LP's named investment advisor or authorised agent must complete an in-person bank interview at a branch; remote online opening is not a standard product for partnership accounts and is generally rejected by Tier-1 banks where a non-resident beneficial owner holds more than a minor economic interest. Acceptable substitute on a discretionary basis: notarised physical verification of identity and signature completed by a Canadian notary public, certified copies of all LP registry documents, and a subsequent video call with the relationship manager.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: BC limited partnership with non-resident beneficial ownership structured in a way that could conceal the ultimate economic owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified BC Registry limited-partnership registration excerpt; complete limited partnership agreement with capital-contribution and UBO schedule; registered-office confirmation; full identification (valid passport or national ID), residential address, date of birth, nationality, and profit-share percentage of every limited partner; source-of-funds evidence for partner capital contributions; professional reference letter from the General Partner's home-country licensed attorney or corporate service provider; tax-residency certificate or NR6/treaty disclosure where a non-resident partner claims relief.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual volume of cross-border recurring SaaS card payments flowing into a newly formed entity, triggering cash-velocity or geographic-mismatch monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe settled-transaction statements and merchant file; standard SaaS terms and executed customer contracts; PCI DSS Level 1 and ISO 27001 attestation; board or GP resolution identifying the payment-rail design; interim financial statements and partner capital ledger demonstrating business purpose; explanation of revenue-recognition accounting under IFRS 15.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty geographies in the legal document and e-signature workload include sanctions-sensitive jurisdictions or politically exposed persons.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal AML/ATF compliance policy; risk-based customer due-diligence manual; sanctions-screening outputs against UN, EU, OFAC, and CBSA lists; PIPEDA privacy-impact assessment; technology-export classification memo confirming that the e-signature SaaS is not on Canada's Export Control List; KYB file for each material law-firm and corporate customer; quarterly transaction-monitoring report.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident limited-partner capital should be wired via SWIFT MT103 (or Fedwire/CHIPS for USD from the United States) to the LP's Schedule-I bank operating account under a clear payment reference, for example 'Capital contribution - LPA clause 7.2 - PIA-001 - Partner name', together with a General Partner capital-call resolution retained in the bank file. Each injection of C$10,000 or more is reportable as an Electronic Funds Transfer Report to FINTRAC, with same-beneficiary aggregation across a 24-hour window. No Canadian regulatory approval is required to inject capital into a non-control SaaS business; however, the non-Canadian founders must file the Investment Canada Act s.12 new-business notification with Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada within 30 days of establishment, maintain the notification number in the corporate book, and avoid future acquisition activity that would cross the WTO review threshold. Escrowed capital should be pre-segregated in a non-interest-bearing account to simplify partner-level tax allocation and to support the LP's pass-through tax posture.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursements for the LegalTech SaaS model should be executed over: (i) SWIFT MT103 for non-CAD vendor invoices, cloud-infrastructure payments, and law-firm disbursements; (ii) Lynx high-value wire for CAD transactions above C$100,000; (iii) Payments Canada ACSS batch ACH and Real-Time Rail (RTR) for recurring low-value CAD settlements, payroll, and supplier credits; and (iv) a commercial letter of credit under UCP600 only if a counterparty insists on trade-finance protection, which is outside the standard SaaS treasury. Card-brand treasury is handled through Stripe's Canadian acquiring and settlement route into the Schedule-I operating account. Every foreign disbursement must carry a precise business-purpose narrative, be supported by an invoice in the vendor file, and be reviewed for Part XIII and Regulation 105 withholding where services are performed in Canada by a non-resident contractor (NR4 and T4A-NR filings) and for treaty-reduced withholding on software-licence or royalty elements. Related-party disbursements must be supported by transfer-pricing documentation consistent with s. 247 of the Income Tax Act and the arm's-length principle.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD outright FX forward contracts executed with a Schedule-I bank dealing room under an IFEMA 2004 or ISDA 2002 master agreement, limited to hedging forecast card settlement collections and known operational exposures.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for remittance of SaaS receipts from non-convertible or restricted emerging-market currencies; the CAD is fully convertible, so CAD NDFs are neither required nor standard.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CAD/USD) with matched maturity to offset long-duration cloud-infrastructure cost liabilities against partner capital contributions, subject to the BC Derivatives Act end-user exemption and mandatory trade-reporting obligations where applicable.
Purchased premium-paid vanilla OTC FX options, being CAD/USD puts and calls, used strictly as protective coverage; the writing of uncovered options is excluded from the LP treasury policy.
Short-dated FX swaps against CAD for temporary cross-currency liquidity bridges executed through the Bank of Canada settlement framework and a Schedule-I bank, not for speculative profit-taking.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Limited Partnership Annual Report (Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: British Columbia Corporate Registry / Registrar of Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: due within two months after the registration anniversary date; no fixed calendar day.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the annual report is not filed for two consecutive years, the Registrar may cancel the LP registration; the partnership loses the benefit of limited liability status and restoration requires filing all missed returns plus additional restoration fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and prescribed schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a fiscal period ending on December 31, due March 31 of the following calendar year; for a non-calendar fiscal period, due by the last day of the fifth month after the fiscal period end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or missing T5013 filings may expose the partnership and its partners to daily late-filing penalties up to CAD 2,500 (approx. USD 1,850), with additional criminal or civil penalties for intentional failure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general statutory audit requirement is imposed on a British Columbia limited partnership under the Limited Partnership Act. An independent audit is compulsory only if the partnership is a reporting issuer under securities legislation, or if the partnership agreement, lender, or regulator specifically requires audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) is the typical benchmark for a privately held LP; International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) applies if the entity or the general partner is publicly accountable, a reporting issuer, or if voluntary adoption is chosen under partnership agreement.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No public beneficial-ownership registry filing is currently required for a private BC limited partnership. Annual confirmation is performed via partner representation letters and KYC refresh on any capital event. Partner changes must also be reflected in the T5013 allocation schedules filed with CRA.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Record of Contributions and Profit/Loss Allocations

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 220-450 USD per year for a registered office and registered agent service in British Columbia
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutorily required; if contracted voluntarily, 5,000-15,000 USD for a small LegalTech SaaS limited partnership

stage_6.statutory_headline_rate: 27% combined general (15% federal Part I general rate + 12% British Columbia provincial general rate); fiscally transparent BC LP allocates income to partners for taxation at partner-level rates
stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal SR&ED refundable ITC at 35% of qualified expenditures (CCPC partners) or 15% (non-CCPC partners) allocated through the LP; BC provincial SR&ED credit at 10% refundable; small business deduction is unavailable to the LP itself but available to corporate Canadian partners on their share of active business income up to CAD 500,000 (federal) / CAD 500,000 (BC) annual limit, producing an 11% combined small business rate; payments for e-signature/SaaS exports to non-residents are zero-rated for GST purposes (export of services)
